facts.text: MET Weather Station & Laser Lidar was deployed at Vastitas Borealis during Phoenix in 2008.
Canadian Space Agency meteorological station with temperature and pressure sensors and a dual-wavelength neodymium-YAG laser lidar that fired green pulses 20 kilometres up into the arctic atmosphere.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Observed water-ice clouds 4 km high and directly detected snow falling from Martian clouds, sublimating before reaching the ground (virga).
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Vastitas Borealis.
Proved that precipitation and active hydrological cycles exist in the contemporary Martian atmosphere.
